#156220. Tech Report: Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2266 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Womenshealthmag ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Your Guide to Running on the Treadmill This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2266 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill.
  • There was more snow and ice on the ground in Newly introduced York City than I had seen in a long time, but I had a half-marathon to train for.
  • But, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there’s almost no other cardio machine that brings up as many feelings as the treadmill. For the first few years of my running career, I’d do just about everything I could to avoid hopping on one, even if that meant running in freezing temps or heavy rain.

Then, last winter happened. There was more snow and ice on the ground in Newly introduced York City than I had seen in a long time, but I had a half-marathon to train for. It left me no choice: I had to move my workouts to the treadmill unless I wanted to end up like that meme where the woman says snow is the perfect texture for running just to wipe out on live television a few seconds later.

But, as any treadmill hater knows, moving a run indoors isn’t as simple as it sounds. A lot changes on a tread—form, mental stimulation, pace—and it can totally mess with your head. Once you understand why, though, it’s a lot easier to work with the treadmill instead of against it; here’s how.

Because it is! For starters, your form changes. “Many people shorten their stride on the treadmill—me included,” states Amy Woods, a USAT-certified run coach and ISSA-certified strength and conditioning coach. “We also tend to run a little more upright.”.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a simple reason behind it. When you’re running outside, your legs have all the space they need for each stride, but on a treadmill, you’re contained to the length and width of the belt. Plus, most people tend to stick too close to the front of the tread, making their space even smaller, states Morgan Mowers, PT, DPT, a physical therapist and V.02-certified run coach.

It has been revealed that between a shortened stride and the fact that it’s a bit easier to propel yourself forward when you’ve got the help of the moving belt, you end up using different muscles on a treadmill compared to outdoors. “We see a decrease in activation of hamstrings and glutes, those bigger propellers that push you forward,” Mowers notes. Instead, you’re seeing more activation in your hip flexors, quads, calves, and knees.

On paper, a lot of these differences should actually make treadmill running easier than running outside. Another example? A treadmill provides a consistent surface. Outside, terrain and incline can vary with each step, so you call on more stabilizing muscles in your ankles and calves, Mowers says. “With every step, there's a little bit of a change when you're running outside versus on a treadmill,” she says. “Even if you are changing up the incline, it's the same exact surface over and over again.” You also don’t have to deal with the same environmental challenges—like heat and wind resistance—that come with running outside. There’s even a famous 1996 study that claims runners should set their incline to 1 percent to accommodate for the difference.

Even with all these easier-sounding differences, running on a treadmill often feels anything but. For many people, myself included, slowing down on a treadmill is the norm. One possible reason: You may just not be used to it, Woods says. Running safely on a treadmill, especially at higher speeds, takes practice. “It's definitely a different feeling when you're running on a treadmill,” Woods says. “You have to be more aware of your foot placement, your arm swing, and where your eyes are looking.” Even if you’re not consciously aware of it, your proprioception (your ability to sense your body’s position in space) could be affected.

Sources indicate that plus, when you’re on the treadmill, you’re stuck at one pace unless you change it, Mowers points out. “That consistency that your body is feeling on a treadmill can make it feel harder, and also may result in you going at an overall slower pace,” she states. When you hop on a treadmill, you start yourself at a pace and settle in until you physically change it. Over the course of a mile outdoors, in comparison, you may start at an 11:00 pace, then speed up to a 10:45 pace for most of it, and end up cruising at a 10:30 pace—all without really noticing. Even though your effort feels the same, your outdoor mile ends up faster.

According to recent reports, then there’s the mental side of things. Outside, you’ve got much more stimulation, says Rachelle Reed, PhD, an exercise physiologist. Your surroundings can offer the perfect distraction, and the natural variations in scenery, incline, terrain, and pace can help keep your brain more engaged too. This can have an impact on your rate of perceived exertion (RPE), Reed says. In fact, a 2019 meta-analysis found that at faster speeds, runners rated their effort as harder on a treadmill compared to outdoors. Basically, it’s harder to go hard on the tread. And because running on a treadmill is technically easier than running outdoors because you have less variation, wind resistance, and environmental factors to navigate at any given moment, that higher RPE really speaks to the mental effects of being inside, Reed says.

It has been revealed that the good news? All these differences between treadmill and outdoor running only really matter if you’re training for a race. That’s because come race day, you’ll want your muscles fully prepped to accommodate your outdoor stride, along with the ability to run across inconsistent terrain and in various elements, Mowers says. Meanwhile, if you’re just looking to do cardio, you can take your pick between the two.

In a recent development, if you are in fact training for a race, how should a treadmill fit into your training? In this case, going outside tends to be superior to staying in, our experts agree. Don’t move your run to the tread at just any sign of inconvenience—running in the rain, cold, and (reasonable) heat all make you a better runner, and you never know if those conditions will pop up on race day, so you’ll be glad to have the practice.

Still, there are definitely situations where it’s not a good idea to go outside. Mowers draws the line when it comes to safety: If the ground is icy, snowy, or slippery in any way, she’ll stay inside to avoid potential injury. If temps are dangerously hot, she’ll run on the treadmill. If there’s risk from serious weather, like thunder and lightning or flooding, she’ll also stay safe indoors. And, she’ll stick to her tread in the event of poor air quality (anything that’s an air quality index over 101).

It’s always worth considering personal safety, too. If your only window to run is late at night and you feel more comfortable staying indoors, do that.

Recent findings suggest that how hot is too hot? This is going to vary down to the person and place. Anything above 85 degrees can be dangerous, Woods states, and you also need to factor in dew point, humidity, and the effort of your run. (Harder efforts are more risky than easier ones.) If temps are higher and you decide to run outdoors, make sure you bring plenty of hydration and fuel, go slower than normal, and pay attention to signs of overheating.

It has been revealed that there’s also the convenience factor. You may need to do a run on the treadmill because it’s more accommodating to your schedule or childcare needs. That’s totally okay too. Ideally, the majority of your runs (we’re talking about 80 percent, and especially your long runs) will be outside, but if you’re someone who finds themselves needing to do the bulk of their running indoors, a run coach can help you make sure you’re prepped for race day. (Woods works with athletes who do the bulk of their training on treads—it’s possible!) The treadmill exists for a reason, and your training will not be affected by the occasional indoor run.

First and foremost, don’t be too hard on yourself about pace. “I always disconnect from pace on the treadmill,” Woods says. Instead, she focuses on her time and RPE. It’s really about thinking about the “spirit of the workout,” she says. For example, you can pay attention to what heart rate zone or effort level you’re supposed to get to and match that—even if that looks slower and feels harder indoors.

And, no, you don’t need to set your incline to 1 percent to compensate for bringing your workout indoors, our experts agree. The biggest reason? The study that established the idea was very small (it had just nine participants) and done only in men. That said, the incline buttons will become useful depending on the kind of run you have on deck for the day.

Finally, give yourself a good warm-up on the treadmill, Mowers states. “Just the act of getting on a treadmill is going to increase our heart rate a little bit because we're a hamster on a wheel; we're trying not to fall off of this thing, and we're so aware of the fact that we're running,” she says. You may need at least 10 to 15 minutes to settle in before getting started with the rest of your workout.

Here’s how to approach different kinds of runs indoors.

Nothing really has to change, Woods claims. It may take you a little longer to run a 5K on your treadmill, but try to stick to the appropriate lower heart rate zones and RPE that you’d normally achieve on these kinds of runs outdoors.

You can play with incline if you’d like—but it’s not a requirement if this is a one-off run you’re doing inside. Running for one day on a completely flat surface won’t affect your training. One reason you may want to try changing the incline may simply be because it adds some variety and stimulation, Woods indicates. If you’re someone who struggles because the treadmill feels boring, try increasing the incline anywhere from 1 to 4 percent for anywhere from 30 seconds to a few minutes every so often.

Sources indicate that another hack: Every 10 minutes, increase your speed slightly. That should give you enough time to warm up a little each time and settle into the pace, so you shouldn’t see much of a jump in demand on your heart rate or effort.

This one gets a bit trickier, Woods notes. Going at all-out speeds on a treadmill can be much tougher—and not feel super safe. This is a time when you’ll want to think about the spirit of the workout. If you have intervals where you’re supposed to get to max heart rate efforts, instead of turning up the speed super high, you can increase the incline in addition to adjusting the speed slightly, Woods says. That should still get you to your zone 4 or 5, all while allowing you to stay slower and feel more in control. This is much easier to accomplish in a tempo run (where you’re holding the pace for longer chunks of time) compared to intervals, so you could also swap an interval run for tempo too.

Industry observers note that you also have the option to skip a speed workout, Woods notes. Missing one session won’t have an impact on your training, and if you’d rather not do it on the treadmill, you also have the option to switch it with another run for the week.

Now, here’s a workout that translates pretty well to the treadmill: All you have to do is up your incline for the duration marked in your workout. Woods recommends sticking between 1 and 4 percent as a good rule of thumb, but you can always bump up to 5 to 8 as long as you can keep good run form.

Ideally, you can move your long run to another day when you can run outside. But, if not, go by time—not mileage. Woods doesn’t recommend running on a treadmill for longer than two hours unless you are very experienced on one because of how it affects your form.

You also have the option to break up your run and do 90 minutes in the morning and 90 minutes in the afternoon. “This will help with form deterioration which is more noticeable and can be more dangerous on a tread,” Woods indicates.

While you’re on your long run, you’ll also want to incorporate moments of incline running and even some pace variation—both for improving your running and also giving yourself a mental reset. Woods also loves to sprinkle in 15- to 30-second walking breaks every mile or so to reset her form and hydrate.

Then the world is really your oyster on the treadmill, but all the same ideas apply: Focus on time and effort, not pace. And, feel free to sprinkle in different inclines and speeds to work different heart rate zones and find moments of mental reset.

Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup in a huge way with the launch of OPTIMUS, an all-upcoming, go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle that packs over 100 equivalent hp and a 40 mph top speed.

Industry observers note that first shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the newly redesigned Greenworks OPTIMUS UTV is the biggest, baddest, and newest addition to the organization’s battery-backed commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims the newly introduced SxS brings together the brand’s purpose-built equipment and power platforms and is designed to work across the demands of its professional property maintenance customers.

“OPTIMUS has always been about pushing battery power beyond what the industry expects, and the UTV is a natural extension of that vision,” says Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks. “We’re bringing professionals more ways to put battery power to work, from the equipment they use to maintain properties to the utility vehicles and charging systems that support their entire operation.”.

Industry observers note that greenworks’ OPTIMUS is built around the firm’s 400V high-voltage electrical platform and mates a pair of compact electric motors that combine for 110 equivalent (?) hp. Those motors draw power from a 19 kWh lithium-ion battery pack with enough efficiency to hit a 40 MPH top speed and cover up to 68 miles of range under typical operating conditions.

When it’s time to haul, OPTIMUS offers buyers a 2,500 lb. towing capacity and 1,300 lb. payload capacity along with 11 full inches of ground clearance and a beefy, 6,000 lb. electric winch. Independent suspension, oversized all-terrain tires, torque vectoring differentials, and multiple terrain modes round out the spec sheet and a picture of a machine that’s designed to handle some seriously demanding off-road applications.

Looks expensive but for a gov or firm leasing or buying a latest utv probably price completive with less headache.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BNB Chain has outlined the architecture for a latest Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 (L1) network, confirming that the proposed framework will not introduce a separate native token.

In an H2 2026 Tech Roadmap published in July 2026, BNB Chain stated that a next-generation L1 architecture was in development on a design path toward the 1 million TPS end-of-life goal and toward supporting different use cases than the existing ones. The plan was to ship it on testnet by the end of 2026, with mainnet release following in early 2027.

Fast forward to the close of November 2026, BNB Chain has introduced the Litepaper for the Newly introduced L1, which describes the architecture being developed for high-frequency trading, payments, private finance and autonomous AI agents.

The design combines early transaction feedback, reserved capacity, native account controls and shielded settlement.

The fresh L1 complements BNB Smart Chain, keeps BNB as its native network token with no new native token, and extends BNB's utility into trading, payments, privacy, and AI scenarios while staying interoperable with the BNB Chain ecosystem.

The latest L1 is being developed alongside BNB Smart Chain, which remains the ecosystem’s broad-based network and streams small groups of transactions called SubBlocks before sealing a full block, with its public testnet being worked towards.

On the upcoming L1, lanes reserve a share of block capacity for eligible activity, such as payments, while unused capacity returns to general traffic. This reduces competition from unrelated activity without guaranteeing that every transaction lands immediately.

It has been revealed that the design also reduces the work of recording changes to the chain’s state. The new L1’s privacy design supports shielded settlement for BNB and admitted BEP-20 tokens. Through AtomicCall, shielded assets can fund selected public operations, such as supported swaps.

The newly introduced L1 retains an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)-compatible execution environment. Parallel EVM execution is planned, and protected ordering through a trusted execution environment (TEE) gateway has also been proposed.

BNB Chain invites the crypto community to participate in discussions on its Layer 1,  submitting their questions, use cases, and feedback to the BNB Forum.

  • Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.
  • Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a new initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets.

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a new initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

Sources indicate that as cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s new VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

It has been revealed that the initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

It has been revealed that the exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular users and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, said, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our users engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”.

Both new and existing Binance customers can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, owners can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

The program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance users.

The additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Customers who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bit Digital sold $50 million in Ethereum to repay a loan that helped finance its AI infrastructure expansion, but its remaining debt leaves the company's crypto treasury exposed to further financial pressure.
  • According to recent reports, the Ethereum treasury company disclosed on Nov.
  • According to recent reports, the sale marks a reversal of Bit Digital's original financing strategy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bit Digital sold $50 million in Ethereum to repay a loan that helped finance its AI infrastructure expansion, but its remaining debt leaves the company's crypto treasury exposed to further financial pressure.

According to recent reports, the Ethereum treasury company disclosed on Nov. 25 that it sold 29,825 ETH between Nov. 15 and 23 at an average price of $1,676, using the proceeds to halve its outstanding debt to Galaxy Digital to $50 million.

According to recent reports, the sale marks a reversal of Bit Digital's original financing strategy. The company borrowed against its Ethereum holdings to help fund the expansion of its AI infrastructure subsidiary, WhiteFiber, while retaining exposure to ETH.

However, Bit Digital does not expect WhiteFiber to fully repay its bridge loan until the second quarter of 2027, while its agreement with Galaxy allows the lender to demand additional collateral within 24 hours.

Bit Digital borrowed against staked ETH to fund its AI infrastructure subsidiary.

The WhiteFiber bridge remained outstanding after Bit Digital paid down its Galaxy loan.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

According to recent reports, the arrows show the direction of the original lending. The bars share a $100 million principal scale and compare Bit Digital’s reported Galaxy balances immediately before and after the November repayment.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

Kairos Research found that the value of the Ethereum collateral backing Bit Digital's $100 million Galaxy loan had fallen to about 131% of the outstanding principal as the company began moving ETH for sale.

The research firm tracked approximately 24,800 ETH moving through Galaxy's hot wallet into Coinbase deposit addresses before Bit Digital publicly confirmed the sale, which ultimately accounted for around 18% of its Ethereum treasury.

During the period in which Galaxy delivered the ETH to Coinbase, Bit Digital's shares fell 15%, compared with a 4% decline in Ethereum.

Following the repayment, Bit Digital reported holdings of approximately 134,532 ETH and ETH equivalents, including 69,089 LsETH pledged against its remaining Galaxy debt and 36,811 ETH staked directly on Ethereum.

The pledged LsETH represents a substantial portion of the firm's remaining treasury, leaving its financial position sensitive to further declines in Ethereum's price.

Under the master loan agreement, Galaxy can demand additional collateral when the value of pledged assets falls below an agreed threshold.

Bit Digital ordinarily has 24 hours from the issuance of that notice to provide additional collateral, although individual loan terms can impose shorter deadlines.

In a recent development, the organization's quarterly filing also disclosed that its outstanding Galaxy borrowing at the end of September was callable on seven days' notice. The repayment announcement did not specify whether that provision applies to the remaining $50 million.

These obligations leave Bit Digital potentially needing to raise capital well before WhiteFiber returns the money it borrowed.

WhiteFiber's ability to repay its parent firm could depend partly on its progress securing funding for the NC-1 data center.

In a recent development, on Nov. 9, WhiteFiber subsidiaries entered into a $300 million project financing agreement with a lender group represented by Morgan Stanley Senior Funding.

The agreement provides an initial $200 million facility, with funding conditions including operational readiness and customer acceptance of the data center's first 40 megawatts of capacity. WhiteFiber reported that no loans had been funded as of Nov. 10.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, consumers will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is key to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.

The 8 Best Standing Desks for Walking Pads, Tested and Reviewed

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • You log a lot of time at your desk, making it fair to wonder how to create a workspace that’s as comfortable and healthy for you as possible.
  • While TikTok is packed with happy-looking people working this way, the treadmill desk is more than a trend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

You log a lot of time at your desk, making it fair to wonder how to create a workspace that’s as comfortable and healthy for you as possible. If sitting on your butt all day isn’t your idea of a good time, it makes sense to consider investing in a walking pad. To create a seamless workspace, you’ll need a special desk to go with that. The best standing desks for walking pads allow you to cruise along as you work, while still providing all the usual trappings you expect from a desk.

While TikTok is packed with happy-looking people working this way, the treadmill desk is more than a trend. Research ties sitting all day with a higher risk of developing back pain and even complications with cardiovascular health, making it a good idea to try to get up and move as much as possible during your day.

Industry observers note that “Prolonged sitting has been linked to a number of health concerns, which is why many people are turning to standing desks,” indicates Andrew J. Bach, DO, a physiatrist at Cedars-Sinai Spine Center in Los Angeles “A standing desk allows you to get your usual computer-based work done while on your feet, and it comes with several benefits over sitting all day.” (He lists off better circulation, less strain on your back, more calories burned, and better digestion as just a few.).

But proper form is critical with these. “People should keep in mind how long they have been in a certain position, and their posture specifically,” claims Meg Darmofal, DPT, a physical therapist at Michigan State University. You don’t want to shrug your shoulders, reach too far forward, bend over, or crane your neck up or down to see your screen, she says—all of those can put you at risk for developing aches and pains.

To find the best standing desks for walking pads, we consulted experts and had Women's Health editors test several popular models in their own workspaces. Our top pick is the Uplift Standing Desk V3, thanks to its easy height adjustments, customizable design, and compatibility with a walking pad. Ahead, find our favorite options for different budgets, spaces, and work-from-home setups.

Industry observers note that while everyone has different needs in a standing desk, the Uplift V3 is packed with enough features and adjustability to make it a good fit for most. This motorized desk has a height range of 22.6 to 48.7 inches and comes in a wide range of tabletop widths and desktop styles, giving you plenty to choose from.

The desk has an impressive 355-pound lifting capacity, so you can pile a lot on it. WH copyeditor Deanna Martin tested the V3 alongside a walking pad and loved how easily the setup transformed her home office. The desk moves up and down with the touch of a keypad, making it easy to switch between sitting, standing, and walking throughout the workday.

Sources indicate that martin also liked the customizable accessories, which include storage options and even a hammock. There's also a companion app that tracks your standing progress and estimated calorie burn, though you'll need a Bluetooth adapter to connect it to the desk. Best of all, she found the entire setup super easy to assemble.

At over $600, the V3 is certainly an investment. But its versatile design, smooth height adjustments, and 15-year warranty are worth the price point.

Read more: Best Home Office Chairs.

Recent findings suggest that it’s fair to expect to pay more for a motorized standing desk, but this Flexispot option manages to deliver that important feature with a relatively low price tag. The desk moves between 28 and 47.6 inches, giving you plenty to work with. It also has four height presets operated by an LED control panel, and a relatively roomy desktop space.

Industry observers note that the desk includes a hook for your headphones or bag, allowing you to keep them in close reach while you work. It also can handle 176 pounds of weight, which should be plenty to work with. While it doesn’t have as many features as pricier desks like the Uplift 3, it’s still a solid, sturdy option to support you through your workday and comes much more affordably.

According to recent reports, whether you already have a desk you like or just don’t want to splash out for a totally upcoming model, a standing desk converter can be a good middle ground. This option from Rocelco simply plops on top of your existing table to create a standing desk, so you can use a walking pad without replacing your entire WFH setup.

While some standing desk converters are small, this one can hold up to two large monitors, a laptop, and more. There’s a retractable keyboard tray, although it may not extend far enough for everyone's needs. The height adjustment is manual, but easy to do with the turn of a dial. There’s even a grommet hole to help you organize your cords, giving you a lot of the perks of a standing desk without the full commitment. Just make sure your existing desk and converter are tall enough to accommodate your walking pad.

A contoured standing desk allows you to get in close to your workspace, with an ergonomic design that can help you maintain a comfortable position while walking on a treadmill. This Fully Jarvis desk is sleek and comfortable, with a gently sloping and curved front that feels natural under your arms.

Industry observers note that during testing, we were able to put this desk together promptly. It has a very sturdy feel, which is helpful when you’re walking while using it. The desk also thoughtfully includes an outlet and USB/lightning charger, so you can plug in your computer without having to bend over. The motor adjusts easily, although it can be a little choppy when you move up and down. Overall, we found that it was easy and comfortable to use. It looks and feels like a high-quality desk thanks to its bamboo surface and sturdy steel frame, making this a workspace you’ll use for years.

Read More: Best Home Office Chairs.

Having a little extra storage space can go a long way when you're trying to keep your home office organized. This Sanodesk standing desk features built-in drawers to stash away your office clutter. It's also motorized, so you can easily adjust the height when you want to sit, stand, or hop on your walking pad.

WH Designer Taryn Colbert tested the desk for two weeks and gave it a four out of five. She liked its spacious, easy-to-clean surface and preset heights. “It’s perfect,” she notes, adding that it was “easy to put together for a person thats not very handy.”.

In a recent development, her biggest gripes? She wished the power plug were positioned farther toward the back of the desk, rather than toward the front and side, and would have preferred a long, slim drawer for additional storage.

According to recent reports, this electric standing desk from Veken has a compact design that won't take over your home office, along with a motorized height adjustment system that makes it easy to switch between sitting and standing. There are also programmable height presets, so you don't have to find your preferred position every time.

According to recent reports, WH Fitness Editor Cori Ritchey tested the desk for two to four weeks and gave it a five out of five. She was super impressed by how sturdy it felt, even when raised to its maximum height. “It feels well made for a desk that the buyer assembles (no shaky IKEA feeling here, even when at its max height!),” she says. Ritchey also liked the easy-to-use height adjustments and wide range of positions.

In a recent development, her biggest gripe was the size. While the 36-inch desktop was great for occasional use, she wished she'd gone up a size for everyday work. She also found the textured surface a little tricky to clean after spills.

In a recent development, this walking pad features a removable desktop that attaches to the treadmill's railings, giving you a convenient spot for your laptop or tablet while you clock your steps. WH Lifestyle Director Lindsay Geller tested the setup for over a month and gave it a five out of five. She especially liked how sturdy the desktop felt once attached and how easy it was to remove. “This is a really great way to get a second desk without actually committing to buying a full desk,” she indicates, noting that she shares a home office with her husband. She also found assembly straightforward, putting the entire setup together by herself in about an hour.

Industry observers note that the desk is admittedly basic, and the treadmill doesn't offer adjustable incline. Geller also found the walking surface a little narrow for jogging, making this a better option for walking while working than more intense workouts.

Every standing desk has either a set height or height range. Bach points out that height is a “key factor” in your desk. “If you’re especially tall or short, make sure the desk can adjust to a level that works for you,” he indicates. Just keep in mind that you’ll want to include the height of your walking pad when figuring out the right standing desk height for you, since you’ll be on top of it while you use your desk. “Returning a bulky standing desk can be a hassle, so it’s best to get the right fit from the start,” Bach says. Ideally, your desk should be high enough that you can type comfortably while standing on your walking pad, without having to hunch over or raise your shoulders.

Recent findings suggest that not all standing desks are adjustable, but many are—and it’s a nice feature to have. “Being able to easily lower and raise the desk is notable because, in some scenarios, returning to sitting is good as well,” Darmofal says. Some desks can be heavy and awkward to move manually, which can be frustrating if you plan to switch between sitting and standing during the day, Bach says. “Motorized options are the most convenient, since they transition with the push of a button,” he adds. (Just keep in mind that motorized options tend to cost more.).

Industry observers note that at the end of the day, this is still a desk, and you need one that will hold your stuff. Make sure you factor in space to hold your computer, pens, notepad, water bottle, and anything else you usually have on your desk. If you're using a walking pad, you'll also want enough room for your keyboard and monitor so you don't have to lean forward while walking.

It’s important to make sure that your desk’s legs and any footing are wide enough to leave space for your walking pad to slip between. Pay close attention to the walking pad dimensions and desk dimensions, leaving a little room around the pad so you’re not jamming it in there.

We should also note that a lot of our standing desk selections below don't come with a walking pad (though the Sharper Image Treadmill Desk is an all-in-one option), meaning it's an additional expense. If you don't already have one, make sure to check out our under-desk treadmill buying guide.

In a recent development, I consulted with Bach and Darmofal to help identify what to look for in standing desks for walking pads. From there, I researched top models, narrowing the field based on criteria like comfort, adjustability, and ease of use. Because everyone has a different experience, I also paid close attention to customer reviews and prioritized desks with overwhelmingly positive feedback.

It has been revealed that from there, Women's Health editors put several standing desks to the test in their own workspaces. Our testers included Cori Ritchey, Lindsay Geller, Taryn Colbert, and Deanna Martin, who evaluated the desks for build quality, ease of assembly, adjustability, size, and overall functionality. Testing periods ranged from one week to over a month, with editors using their desks while sitting, standing, or walking on an under-desk treadmill. We also considered how stable each setup felt, how easily it fit into a home office, and any drawbacks our testers encountered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers.

The updated browser workspace adds an in-editor assistant as Solana expands its wider AI developer push.

Solana has rolled out a built-in AI coding agent inside Solana Playground, its browser-based development environment, aiming to help programmers learn, build, and deploy smart contracts without setting up local toolchains.

For traders and investors, it offers useful context on developer onboarding, Solana’s AI infrastructure push, and early-stage protocol risk.

In a post on X, Solana introduced the updated Solana Playground as a place to “learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser,” noting that the integrated agent explains existing code and edits it alongside the developer rather than writing full programs on its own.

Introducing Solana Playground – where you learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser. An AI agent explains the code and edits it with you. Start here: https://t.co/nM0ySqDkfO pic.twitter.com/SFKYYTx04n.

Builders can start projects using either Anchor, a framework that streamlines Solana program development, or native Solana programming, which offers lower-level control without framework abstractions.

According to product walk-throughs, the workspace includes three guided learning paths. These include an introductory Anchor tutorial called Hello Anchor and an intermediate build named Lumberjack. It also offers 10 sample Solana programs.

Browser-based Solana development predates the AI integration: the open-source Solana Playground (SolPg) has long let developers compile Rust programs, manage development wallets, and deploy contracts without a local CLI setup.

The latest release adds an in-editor assistant to explain unfamiliar code and apply edits within the same session.

The Playground enhancement fits into a wider push around AI and automated agents on Solana.

Solana’s developer portal now provides guidance for AI coding agents, while solana.ai focuses on autonomous trading, wallet management, and stablecoin payments.

The Solana Foundation has also introduced an open-source Confidential Compute toolkit with Nito for AI workloads involving sensitive data.

Figures shared by the Solana Foundation at Breakpoint 2026 indicated more than 120 teams are building AI products on Solana, with access to the Builder Program for grants, technical resources, hiring support, marketing help, and infrastructure credits.

Sources indicate that developer-focused releases rarely drive sustained moves in SOL or ecosystem tokens on their own. Liquidity, macro conditions, and net capital flows carry far more weight in the near term.

However, lowering the barrier to write and iterate on code can speed up experimentation—and increase the volume of fresh or lightly tested contracts. Developer activity remains a key indicator of long-term ecosystem growth.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, residents of New Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief.
  • According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).
  • The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, residents of New Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief. A dangerous menace to society has been taken off the streets after police apprehended a 75-year-old man accused of leading deputies on a high-stakes electric bike chase at speeds reaching a blistering 16 mph (26 km/h).

According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).

The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.

What followed was apparently the world’s slowest police chase.

Mitchell reportedly continued riding along the beach, eventually exiting onto city streets, where he allegedly rode against traffic before making it back to his home. Deputies followed him, and when Mitchell attempted to retreat into his garage, he reportedly resisted arrest by grabbing onto a golf cart and refusing to let go.

Recent findings suggest that the ordeal ended with Mitchell in custody, facing four charges, including felony fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, resisting an officer without violence, speeding on the beach, and riding outside the designated beach driving area. His bond was set at $4,000.

And just like that, another dangerous electric bicycle criminal was brought to justice. This was clearly a success story like no other, and American streets are now safer.

In a recent development, now, before anyone gets too worked up, let’s be clear: I’m not suggesting that e-bike riders should be allowed to ignore traffic laws, endanger pedestrians, or flee from police. Reports indicate that Mitchell was riding recklessly around beachgoers, including children, and that’s certainly something worth addressing. And once he allegedly decided to flee from deputies, he turned what could have been a minor infraction into a much more serious situation.

But can we also acknowledge how absurd this whole thing is?

We’ve reached a point where a 75-year-old man riding a bicycle at 16 mph can end up the subject of a police pursuit and felony charges, while we’ve largely accepted that multi-ton vehicles routinely kill and seriously injure people on our roads as an unavoidable cost of modern transportation.

Every day, drivers speed through neighborhoods, roll through stop signs, stare at their phones, and operate vehicles capable of killing pedestrians with a moment’s inattention. Or perhaps I shouldn’t say ‘capable’, but rather that they do. 40,000 people every year die in the US from car violence. Yet somehow, electric bicycles have become one of the great transportation menaces of our time, despite contributing much, much less to major bodily harm or death.

In a recent development, and yes, there are absolutely legitimate concerns about dangerous riding. I’ve repeatedly argued that we need better enforcement, especially when it comes to teenagers riding high-powered electric dirt bikes and e-motos at 40 mph (64 km/h) down sidewalks and bike paths. Those aren’t electric bicycles, and treating them as such has created a real problem for everyone.

But if we’re going to devote police resources to cracking down on dangerous two-wheeled behavior, perhaps we could start there instead of turning a 1 mph beach ride into the crime of the century.

According to recent reports, what is absurd is that he didn't simply stop and follow the officer's directions to slow down. If he is going to try to flee from the police by riding dangerously including going against traffic then he should face charges. As presumably a first time offender, he'll be given probation if he agrees not to do it again.

In a recent development, to be fair, Mitchell’s alleged behavior after being stopped certainly didn’t help his case. But the larger point remains: our priorities around road safety have become wildly distorted.

We’ve normalized the dangers of cars so thoroughly that we barely blink at the daily carnage they cause, yet we’re increasingly treating comparatively low-speed electric bicycles as an existential threat to public safety.

Industry observers note that I’m all for enforcing sensible e-bike rules. I’m all for throwing the book at major infractions and scofflaws who pose a public menace. But I’m also for applying a little perspective.

Because if a 75-year-old man riding an electric bicycle at 16 mph is among our most pressing transportation safety concerns, then I have some very good news about the state of our roads. But unfortunately, there is no good news to share today.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that japan’s Financial Services Agency returned to the issue of Bitcoin self-custody in a Nov.
  • An exchange manages the signing keys while it holds Bitcoin for a customer.
  • In a recent development, the Travel Rule requires providers to share information on certain transfers between them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that japan’s Financial Services Agency returned to the issue of Bitcoin self-custody in a Nov. 26 paper for its study group. Japanese exchanges already have to record details of covered withdrawals. The paper asks what can protect customers once they hold the signing keys themselves.

An exchange manages the signing keys while it holds Bitcoin for a customer. In a self-custody wallet, the customer controls the keys needed to authorize a transfer. The FSA’s November discussion paper points out what happens if customers lose access to those keys. They may be unable to move their Bitcoin.

In a recent development, the Travel Rule requires providers to share information on certain transfers between them. An exchange sending Bitcoin to a customer’s own wallet has no receiving provider to notify. On a covered withdrawal, Japan’s recordkeeping rules require the exchange to collect and record details such as the destination wallet owner’s name and wallet address.

It has been revealed that on a covered transfer from a self-custody wallet into the exchange without that notice, the exchange records the information it can obtain. The FSA’s supervisory guidelines cite the rules implementing Japan’s Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds and call for exchanges to examine the wallet’s characteristics and assess its money-laundering risk.

In a recent development, the duties apply to exchanges that handle transfers. When two people transfer Bitcoin directly between wallets they control, neither has an exchange carrying out those checks. Under Switzerland’s planned crypto tax reporting, providers would report transactions they handle, while later transfers between personal wallets would fall outside that reporting.

Two Bitcoin transfer routes show where a Japanese exchange has to keep a record and where owners control the signing keys.

An exchange records details on covered withdrawals. In self-custody, the wallet owner controls the keys.

The exchange example covers outbound transfers without a Travel Rule notice.

The routes illustrate the providers and participants described in the FSA’s transfer explainer and supervisory guidance.

The exchange example covers outbound transfers without a Travel Rule notice.

The November staff paper cites a withdrawal waiting period for upcoming exchange accounts as an example of an anti-fraud measure for a Cabinet Office ordinance. It gives no duration. Japan’s Diet passed amendments to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and the Payment Services Act on July 15. As of Nov. 27, the FSA’s public rulemaking register listed no implementing ordinance or effective date for the proposed delay.

Sources indicate that A February summary of the working group’s recommendations gave an example of how an exchange could intervene before a withdrawal. Immediately after opening an account, a customer could face a waiting period before sending crypto to a wallet they control.

Recent findings suggest that in August, the FSA and Japan’s National Police Agency separately asked the industry’s self-regulatory association to strengthen withdrawal restrictions after cash deposits, crypto purchases or registration of a withdrawal destination. The request also called for scam warnings and transaction monitoring. The agencies also asked exchanges to check customers who make large or frequent withdrawals soon after restrictions lift.

For people who already hold their own keys, the November paper asks how to warn them about wallet risks and where regulation might help if problems arise. It also asks whether further measures are needed to curb money laundering and terrorist financing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you wake up tomorrow as the esteemed Lord Mayor of London, you’ll want to make a properly dignified entrance. To make sure your arrival turns the right heads, Electrogenic has taken the Mayor’s 1973 Roll-Royce Phantom VI and turned it into a properly traditional standard-bearer with modern electric power.

The stately, stylish, and silent electric Rolls-Royce car made its public debut at last month’s Salon Privé weekend at Blenheim Palace, where it joined a growing fleet of classic Rollers that have received Elctrogenic’s electric conversion, including the stunning Mulliner-bodied 1929 Phantom II that we covered back in 2023.

For this project, Electrogenic carefully removed the internal combustion-based engine, transmission, and fuel system from the City of London Corporation’s official ’73 Phantom VI limo and replaced it with a 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motor putting out 310 Nm (~230 lb-ft) of torque. Sharp-eyed readers will note those numbers are significantly lower than what you’d expect from the 6.2L L410 V8 fitted with twin SU carburetors (as it was in the standard ’73 IV), but since those numbers were never officially published, we would say that the power available from the fresh electric drivetrain is similarly adequate for Mayoral use.

Power for the electric motor comes from a 62 kWh li-ion battery fitted under the hood bonnet, and offers more than enough range to get the Lord Mayor to their appointments in and around the city.

To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.

“We were honored to be asked to electrify this significant motor car, and to play a part in the City of London Corporation’s journey to net zero,” notes Steve Drummond, chief executive of Electrogenic. “When it was launched in the late 1960s, the Rolls-Royce VI was the most refined and dignified limousine on the road. Now, thanks to electrification, its core character has been enhanced further: it is whisper quiet, effortless to drive with swift performance, and emits zero tailpipe emissions.”.

It's vital for government to be seen to follow it's own policy.

A standard complaint by oil lobbyists is that government vehicles aren't electrified.

Only 374 Phantom VIs were built between 1968 and 1990, with this 3 meter-long coach-built limousine having been commissioned during the mayoralty of Alderwoman Dame Susan Langley DBE, the 697th Lord Mayor of the City of London. The Phantom was converted as part of the Corporation’s broader effort to achieve a net zero carbon emissions goal from its own operations in 2027.

Home » Trendsetter News » Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA.

Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout links banking activity more directly to NIGHT than ADA, but its £250M bid reflects initial capacity.

The £250 million figure attached to Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout is an initial capacity limit, not confirmed customer deposits, according to a video from crypto commentator FireHustle.

That distinction sits at the heart of the host’s analysis: a bank adopting technology built by Cardano’s developers does not necessarily translate into immediate demand for ADA.

The video describes a savings product that keeps customers’ money in pounds while recording their accounts on Midnight, the privacy-focused blockchain developed by Input Output.

Its potential significance lies less in the headline amount than in which token benefits from the activity.

According to Fire Hustle, Monument’s offering pays existing customers a fixed 5.2% for one year. Account details remain private, and customers cannot sell or transfer the blockchain records, even to another Monument customer.

Cardano’s Founder Charles Hoskinson celebrated the rollout with the phrase “250 million pounds on-chain.” But the host states Monument has not disclosed actual deposits, despite tokens representing the full initial allocation already having been created.

The YouTube video also cites Midnight Foundation president Fahmi Syed saying seven other banks are considering similar products: six in Canada and one in Japan.

Canada merits attention because Calgary-based digital-asset custodian Balance handles Monument’s tokens, according to the video. The host explicitly cautions against assuming the unnamed institutions are Canada’s six largest banks.

Midnight’s token structure is the investment question. The video states holding NIGHT generates DUST, the resource used to pay network transaction fees. Banks or service providers can therefore cover customers’ activity without requiring savers to handle tokens themselves.

It has been revealed that “Somebody still has to hold the Night that makes the Dust,” she claims. That creates a more direct connection between Midnight usage and NIGHT than between that usage and ADA, although additional activity does not guarantee token-price gains.

Sources indicate that the ADA connection is more distant. Cardano stake-pool operators are expected to help secure Midnight in early 2027, with potential rewards extending to their ADA delegators. Those rewards are prospective, not existing income.

It has been revealed that fire Hustle reports ADA trading more than 90% below its peak at recording. However, the more useful indicators are actual Monument deposits, transaction volumes and confirmed bank introduces.

#156195. Raving in Your 40s, 50s, and 60s? These Women Say It’s the Best Self-Care They’ve Found

Raving in Your 40s, 50s, and 60s? These Women Say It’s the Best Self-Care They’ve Found

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that ask Karen Manson, 65, how she likes to recharge, and she’ll tell you this: a night of pounding bass, a sweaty dance floor, and getting home in the wee hours of the morning.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s how she ended up at her first rave last year, solo.
  • Industry observers note that manson isn’t an outlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ask Karen Manson, 65, how she likes to recharge, and she’ll tell you this: a night of pounding bass, a sweaty dance floor, and getting home in the wee hours of the morning. She’s loved music her whole life and was always drawn to EDM, but marrying and having kids young left little room to explore it. Then, three years ago, her husband died, and she began thinking about how short and precious life is—and decided it was time to push herself to try new experiences.

Recent findings suggest that that’s how she ended up at her first rave last year, solo. She was nervous, but spent the night dancing, and left with new friends and a newfound confidence. “I felt uninhibited,” she states. She’s attended more than 20 raves since.

Industry observers note that manson isn’t an outlier. Midlife women are prioritizing their mental health now more than ever, according to a 2026 study in the journal Women’s Health that analyzed nearly 1,000 surveys about women’s health priorities and concerns. And a number of them are finding relief on the dance floor.

A 2025 study in Psychology of Music surveyed 136 women ages 40 to 65 about why they’re involved in EDM experiences. The overwhelming response was that raving was a meaningful part of their mental well-being—an outlet for stress, a source of connection, and a rare place to escape the demands of everyday life, according to the survey.

In a recent development, “There is a rise in older people attending electronic dance music events, raves, clubs, parties, festivals,” says Alice O’Grady, PhD, a professor of applied performance at the University of Leeds, who co-authored the Psychology of Music study. “The motivations for women going are pretty much characterized as the same as they are for any age: the love of the music, the ability to socialize with existing friends, the atmosphere of the environment, and the sense of community.” Put simply: These music events are plain fun.

The EDM scene is no longer the epitome of youth culture, O’Grady adds, and it’s become more socially acceptable for women to embrace this genre of joy as they get older. That shift may reflect changing attitudes about aging, with women potentially feeling less constrained by traditional expectations about how they’re “supposed” to spend their time as they age. Social media has also made it much easier to discover niche music scenes, while a growing focus on mental health, movement, pleasure, and community may be encouraging women to seek out experiences that just make them feel good.

The older you get, the harder it can be to find a place where you can be playful, spontaneous, and fully present with other people. For some, the rave scene provides exactly that. “You've got more responsibility, more commitments,” O’Grady says. “You want that escape, you want that ability to connect through music and immerse yourself in an environment that allows you to be expressive and just shake off some of those roles that older women carry.”.

Samantha Hillery, 43, started raving in her 20s as a way to let loose and have fun. But as life got busier with work, family, and kids, she stopped going. Years later, while searching for fun things to do in her area with friends, she came across Bingo Loco, a high-energy party with EDM, dancing, confetti, and—yes—bingo, and found her way back to it.

Now, Hillery gives herself permission to step away from the endless list of adult responsibilities. “As we get older and super busy with our lives, we forget how fun we maybe used to be, and it seems like something that was so far in the past,” she says. “But when you’re able to go out and rave surrounded by a bunch of friends and people that just want to have a good time, you remember that part of you isn’t lost.”.

For some, keeping up with friends also becomes more challenging as you age and enter fresh eras of your life. Social obligations often come second, competing with work schedules, children, relationships, and other obligations, notes Madison Liddle, LMHC, a licensed psychotherapist at Madison Liddle Therapy and co-founder of The Practice Co, a co-working space for therapists. At a music event like these, though, spontaneous connection is built into the experience.

Sources indicate that hundreds or thousands are gathered around the same music, moving to the same rhythm, creating an immediate sense of belonging. It’s a concept called collective effervescence, which is “a feeling of joy and connection when a group of people are in a shared space doing a shared thing,” Liddle explains. “Social connection is a really strong determinant of health as we age, and raving offers an opportunity to create and be in community with people with shared interests.”.

Getting out and meeting upcoming people is the main reason Manson is so attracted to rave culture—she’s found the crowds to be welcoming and friendly. “Life can become quite small if you don't push yourself,” she says, alluding to feeling alone after her husband’s passing. “I enjoy meeting people, I enjoy conversations. I'm not good at home in my own organization—I need socialization.” Dancing with new friends is the way to do that, and it keeps her feeling energized.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, in Manson’s experience, the EDM scene has seemed remarkably friendly to people of all ages and backgrounds. O’Grady agrees: “Women need spaces that are inclusive, welcoming, and accessible, and the rave scene actually does that quite well,” claims O’Grady. You’ll feel a sense of belonging, like you’re part of something bigger than yourself, even if you’re there alone, she adds. The music creates an instant common language, while dancing alongside friends and strangers turns what could be an individual activity into something meaningful and collective.

Industry observers note that the physical perks of dancing are well documented. It strengthens the cardiovascular, metabolic, musculoskeletal, and cognitive systems, as WH previously reported. It can also improve coordination, balance, and stability, which becomes especially key with age. But it can boost your mental health too, mainly because it helps you stay present. When you’re fully focused on what you’re hearing, feeling, and doing, there’s less room to get caught up in the mental replaying and worrying that can fuel stress, Liddle states.

Sources indicate that in fact, many participants in the Psychology of Music study described dancing at raves as a way to ease anxiety, depression, and low moods, notes co-author Alinka Greasley, PhD, a professor of music psychology at the University of Leeds. Anxiety can keep the mind focused on what might go wrong, while depression can make the present feel flat.

Raving, by contrast, demands attention in a different way. Instead of sitting with your thoughts, you’re listening to loud, immersive music, dancing to the beat, and anticipating the next drop, Liddle explains. That physical engagement helps interrupt rumination and creates a sense of clarity that lasts beyond the dance floor; it can help clear your head.

In a recent development, alex Daly attended her first EDM show at 40 after her partner, who’d been going to raves for years, encouraged her to come along. A year later, raving has become a central part of her wellness routine. If she’s having a stressful week and doesn’t have an EDM show on her calendar, she immediately starts looking for one. “Once I’m in the crowd, I get into a flow state, and moving my body to the beat really helps me process my emotions,” claims Daly, now 41. “Dancing helps me stop ruminating, get out of my head, and back into my body.” For a few hours, there’s simply less room for the mental noise of everyday life. In a way, it’s like the pounding beat is a reset button you can dance to.

Sources indicate that of course, rave culture has long been tied to recreational drugs like MDMA, which can bring on feelings of euphoria, connection, and stress relief. That link hasn’t disappeared. Some of the women in the Psychology of Music study noted they took drugs, often to keep their energy up for dancing, while others went purely for the music and the movement.

In a recent development, however, drugs weren’t what gave the women a sense of belonging, the study uncovered. “That's very much already there from their perspective,” Greasley states. “The drugs are more to do with [increasing] energy levels and also the marrying of the drugs and the music. Many women called it a spiritual experience to be in ecstatic states whilst dancing to the music.”.

Karen D., 62, who asked that her last name be withheld because she discusses her drug use, sees it the same way. She started going to raves in her early 50s with her second husband. While she partakes in recreational drug use, she also knows people who attend raves completely sober. For her, the bonding comes from dancing with like-minded people who are all just happy to be there.

But Karen acknowledges that drugs heighten those feelings and add to the mental health boost she gets from raving. “I feel like my brain’s reconnecting in ways that it has forgotten how to connect,” she notes. “I can get down with what’s going on in my life at times, and it completely transforms me into a much more positive person.”.

Wellness advice in your 40s, 50s, and beyond is often the same advice over and over: protect your sleep, drink less, manage stress, and stick to a routine. But in contrast, this group of ravers finds genuine self-care in the act of staying out late, dancing for hours, and disrupting those prescribed wellness rules. “In this world where everything is so optimized and planned and scheduled, there is something that we lose in terms of fun,” indicates Liddle, noting that raving brings it to the forefront. The key is to accept the occasional trade-off—less sleep in the name of mental health benefits—and to strike a balance between partying and recovering.

In a recent development, manson has attended a couple of Daybreaker events, which are morning, sober parties and raves, often starting around 6 a.m. Early parties like these are becoming more common. O’Grady adds that more women DJs are putting on earlier shows with the attitude of: “We all want to get together, we all want to have a dance, but we want to be in bed by midnight.”.

Industry observers note that however, Manson prefers later reveals because she finds that’s when more traditional EDM is played. But staying up until 4 a.m. at these events has been a bit of a learning curve, so she tries to limit her events to one per weekend. “The enthusiasm's there, but I'm not prepared to spend so much time recovering,” she says. “Once is great, it does what I want it to do. It makes me feel good. I get to connect with people that I enjoy spending time with.” She prioritizes sleeping in the next morning, and just rests the next day if she needs to. Then, she can still go to the gym and take long walks during the week. (She doesn’t work anymore, so she has more flexibility to rest.).

It has been revealed that despite the missed-out-on sleep, Karen D. finds that rave life rejuvenates her. “If I've been away at a festival for a weekend, I come back very tired because I need more sleep,” she says. “However, I do feel refreshed somehow—more clearheaded.”.

In a recent development, but she still makes sure to still get seven hours of sleep if she goes to bed late, so then she can still fulfill her responsibilities at home, like taking her grandson to school. The tradeoff is also worth it for her, and in fact, going to raves inadvertently benefits her wellness routine. It “really helps motivate me to do weight training, to go running, to do all these wholesome recognized exercises, because I want to stay well to be able to go and dance [until] 3 o'clock in the morning,” she says.

Rave culture is no longer just for younger people, and women in midlife are soaking in every ounce of fun, freedom, community, and release. “They don't want to be defined by their age, but more importantly, they don't want to be restricted by it,” claims O’Grady. “Saying, ‘I want to dress up in my sequins, I want to put my face on, I want to go and have a dance, I want to stay out all night and shrug off my responsibilities for a little while, I want all of that and why shouldn't I?’”.

For Manson, getting ready is part of the appeal, and she’s collected a variety of vibrant, fun outfits to go out in. “It's almost like creating a bit of an identity, which I'm quite enjoying,” she claims. At this stage of life, raving has given her a way to reinvent herself.

Midlife can chip away at a woman’s confidence and leave her feeling overlooked. Raving pushes back on that by giving women a place to be bold and seen. As Karen D. puts it, “Women of my age can often disappear or become invisible, and it's almost the opposite of that.”.

Since her husband’s death, Manson has made a point of pushing herself to try new things. Raving has given her lasting memories, a fresh outlook, and a crew of friends who aren’t ready to stop dancing anytime soon. “I live with the feeling that life’s very short and precious,” she claims, “so seize the moment.”.

Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

In a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, mentioned it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

The development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

The Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

As of the latest patch by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are currently being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Patch Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Update Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Patch Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (534 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it.
  • Sources indicate that this vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum.
  • Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it. This, using a payment worth less than $0.35. For context, each planted transaction costs just $0.18 to $0.34, depending on the address format.

Sources indicate that this vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

This is the reason why this revelation has raised an important question about Bitcoin’s privacy — Can someone identify the IP address associated with a Bitcoin wallet, even if the wallet owner never publicly reveals their identity?

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

It has been revealed that to understand the vulnerability, it is vital to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many people operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

According to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node announces the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

Recent findings suggest that on the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Therefore, even watch-only wallets, which monitor addresses without holding their private keys, can be affected. This also means that avoiding address reuse alone may not be enough to protect wallet privacy.

Hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets right now at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.
