Crypto traders who bet on a decline lost nearly $170 million to liquidations over the past 24 hours as Bitcoin, Solana and XRP rose on Black Friday. Short positions made up 68.3% of the $248.8 million in total liquidations.

CoinGlass data showed on Friday that liquidations hit 72,023 traders over that period, and Binance accounted for 44.9% of the total. The largest single order was a $9.3 million BTCUSDT short on Binance, which CoinGlass recorded at a price of $62,147.

In a recent development, bitcoin shorts lost $64.9 million over 24 hours, and Bitcoin longs lost $20.9 million, according to CoinGlass. On the CoinGlass heatmap, shorts made up 75.7% of Bitcoin's $85.8 million in liquidations across all trading pairs. Bitcoin was trading at around $61,400 on Friday, up 0.9% over 24 hours.

CoinGlass recorded $139.6 million of the short liquidations in the past 12 hours, against $29.9 million in long liquidations over the same window.

Sources indicate that ethereum shorts lost $38.1 million, the second-largest amount among all assets on CoinGlass. ETH traded at around $1,721 on Friday, up 1% over 24 hours.

According to CoinGlass, Solana gained 3.3% to around $73, and SOL shorts lost $6 million. XRP rose 1.9% to $0.97, and its shorts lost $2 million.

Sources indicate that on Thursday, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju estimated in a post on X that Bitcoin had about $16 billion in potential short liquidations between $60,000 and $100,000. According to Ju, potential long liquidations below that range totaled less than $5 billion. "The squeeze risk is on the short side," he wrote.

Deribit's monthly Bitcoin options expiry took place at 08:00 UTC on Friday. About 110,800 BTC contracts, worth roughly $6.75 billion, expired with a max pain price of $70,000, according to Deribit data.

Industry observers note that bitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes warned about the weekend in an X post on Friday. "If there is no Fed dovish rhetoric pivot before the pre-FOMC blackout begins EOD Fri US time, this weekend could get spicy," Hayes wrote. He added that liquid assets and crypto could get dumped before Monday's open.

Earlier this week, Hayes said that Bitcoin "will retest $55k" and shared a chart with the price at $58,773. On Nov. 21, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024.

Recent findings suggest that at its October meeting, the Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

Recent findings suggest that the Fed's blackout period starts at midnight ET on Nov. 28, and the FOMC will announce its rate decision on Dec. 9. CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at 100% on Nov. 12.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP.

Ripple’s expansion alone won’t send XRP to $10, a popular wealth coach states.

A $10 XRP would imply a circulating market value of roughly $630 billion, not simply another rally on Ripple announcements.

According to recent reports, that is the central argument from Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, a wealth coach whose latest YouTube video episode examines why the company’s institutional expansion has not translated into the token price many holders expected.

Using approximately 63 billion XRP in circulation, Stevenson argues that reaching that XRP valuation requires more than partnerships and regulatory milestones. It requires sustained demand to own the token, rather than merely move money through it.

Sources indicate that stevenson separates Ripple’s corporate performance, adoption of its products, demand for XRP and the token’s market price. Those categories overlap, but they are not interchangeable: a customer using Ripple’s custody services or stablecoin does not necessarily need XRP.

Sources indicate that even payments routed through XRP may generate limited lasting demand. In the process she describes, a payment provider buys the token, transfers it and sells it into the destination currency within seconds, allowing the same inventory to support repeated transactions.

Sources indicate that “Significant payment numbers alone don’t automatically push the price up,” Dr. Stevenson notes. The more consequential question is how much XRP participants need to keep available between transactions.

According to recent reports, market makers may hold inventory to support larger payment flows, creating a potential link between usage and ownership. Still, the video does not quantify how much additional inventory those flows would require.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson cites roughly 1.19 billion XRP held by ETFs and about 473 million held by Evernorth, a tech giant established to accumulate XRP. Those are figures presented in the video, rather than independently verified current totals.

Her distinction is useful: XRP-backed fund holdings represent direct token ownership, while the national trust bank approval she attributes to Ripple does not itself require institutions to purchase XRP.

In a recent development, supply remains part of the calculation. Stevenson puts Ripple’s escrow holdings at around 31 billion XRP, with up to one billion released monthly and unused amounts returned to escrow. An unlock is therefore not equivalent to an immediate market sale.

It has been revealed that the sharper test is whether an announcement creates incremental buying, how long those tokens stay held and whether fresh supply offsets that demand. Dr. Stevenson remains bullish, but the adoption figures she discusses do not establish when XRP reaches $10.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Bank of England will use a frontier AI scenario in its 2027 operational stress test to see how a disruption involving advanced AI could affect UK finance. One question is whether firms’ recovery plans would work together if several institutions faced disruption at once. The voluntary, exploratory exercise will examine both individual firms and the wider sector.

Recent findings suggest that the Bank set out the initiative for its Cyber and Operational Resilience Stress Test in its Nov. 26 Financial Stability Report. It is discussing possible scenarios with firms, industry groups and technical experts. The Bank plans to invite suitable participants for testing in summer 2027 and publish findings on common themes in the fourth quarter.

The Bank’s Financial Policy Committee record warned that a weakness at a common supplier could disrupt several firms and financial market infrastructure at once. A firm can test how swiftly it would restore its own operations. The committee said risks can remain across the system even when individual firms have credible fallbacks. A Solana routing outage demonstrated how a shared provider can disrupt independently run infrastructure. Validators representing about 29% of stake stopped voting when one provider’s routing failed.

In a recent development, A problem at a shared provider can hit several firms at once. Their separate recovery intends have to work together to keep services running.

Credible fallbacks at individual firms can still leave gaps in the services the sector needs to restore.

Sources indicate that the firms shown are hypothetical. The Bank is still discussing scenarios for the voluntary 2027 frontier AI exercise.

Illustrative network diagram based on the Bank’s discussion of shared providers and collective recovery. Arrows show how disruption and recovery dependencies can connect firms and services.

The firms shown are hypothetical. The Bank is still discussing scenarios for the voluntary 2027 frontier AI exercise.

In its wider resilience work, the Bank is examining whether firms’ workarounds can collectively sustain a minimum level of activity in retail and wholesale payments and sterling interest-rate markets. In those markets, a priority is keeping settlement of UK government bond trades running. That work illustrates the stakes of joint recovery while the Bank weighs scenarios for the AI exercise.

The Bank states a prolonged interruption to retail payments could leave households and businesses unable to make or receive essential payments. In wholesale payments, disruption could tie up cash and collateral and leave firms unsure when incoming payments will arrive, putting pressure on other obligations.

An October survey by the Bank and the Financial Conduct Authority indicates where firms already rely on the same providers. The three largest cloud and computing providers accounted for 79% of reported relationships in that category. The three largest providers of model access and hosting accounted for 54% of reported relationships in theirs.

In a recent development, the survey also found that adoption of AI agents was widespread among respondents and broad autonomy was rare. Among firms that answered the respective questions in the full survey, 80% said they had deployed AI agents and 2% said they had deployed agents with broad autonomy.

The Bank’s stress-test program includes a separate 2026 exercise on disruption involving a cloud provider and third parties, with findings planned for summer 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, most SUVs are lucky to tow a small trailer without breaking a sweat.
  • The Bao 5 made its European debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed (FOS) in July, the first SUV from BYD’s “premium technology-focused” brand, Denza.
  • As Denza’s first SUV designed specifically for Europe, Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, said the tech giant is “confident that the Bao 5 will be a huge hit,” offering the perfect mix of off-road ability, luxury, and advanced technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most SUVs are lucky to tow a small trailer without breaking a sweat. BYD’s upcoming luxury SUV had a slightly bigger challenge: pulling a nearly 400,000-pound jumbo jet. And somehow, it did it on just two wheels. The video is worth a look.

The Bao 5 made its European debut at the Goodwood Festival of Speed (FOS) in July, the first SUV from BYD’s “premium technology-focused” brand, Denza.

As Denza’s first SUV designed specifically for Europe, Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, said the tech giant is “confident that the Bao 5 will be a huge hit,” offering the perfect mix of off-road ability, luxury, and advanced technology.

The SUV uses BYD’s DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) plug-in hybrid powertrain, which BYD remarked is the “world’s first off-road-dedicated hybrid architecture/”.

BYD’s off-road PHEV powertrain features three electric motors (one on each axle and a third generator) and a 1.5L turbocharged engine, delivering a combined 536 horsepower (544 PS) and 560 lb-ft (760 Nm) of torque.

BYD boasted that “Those figures – well clear of PHEV rivals’ and comfortably more than conventional diesel SUVs’ – are enough for a 0-100km/h time of just 4.8 seconds.”.

To top it off, BYD added a double wishbone front and rear suspension with its DiSus-P intelligent body system, plus front and rear intelligent electronic differential locks with millisecond-level response to improve traction and performance.

Industry observers note that the Bao 5 is equipped with a 31.8 kWh BYD Blade Battery that delivers a pure-electric WLTP range of up to 56 miles (90 km). And on a full tank and a full charge, the WLTP combined range is 537 miles (835 km).

To prove the new luxury SUV’s capabilities, BYD put it to the ultimate test — towing a Boeing 747 jumbo jet using just two wheels.

While pulling a 180-tonne, or nearly 400,000-pound, jumbo jet on four wheels is impressive in itself, Denza’s engineers wanted to push it further, doing something never tried before to showcase its off-road DMO technology.

The Bao 5 was put to the test at Dunsfold Aerodrome airfield in Surrey, England. It successfully pulled the jumbo jet in each of its three runs: one on four wheels, one on three, and the last on just two wheels.

Combined, the SUV towed the 747 for a total of 1,600 meters, or close to a mile, which BYD said is about four laps around a standard-size athletic track.

While a feat like this sounds impressive on paper, keep in mind that planes are designed to roll with as little resistance as possible. Top Gear pulled a 747 with a Touareg a while back. The main thing a pushback rig has is weight so that it can maintain traction. That's why BYD put nearly 10,000 lbs of ballast in the back - so it wouldn't spin its wheels on the tarmac.

It's still interesting, to be sure, especially removing two wheels.

BYD mentioned the Bao 5 was a standard, production-spec Ultimate trim model, and the modifications were minimal.

According to recent reports, A towing attachment was added, while the interior passenger seats were removed to make space for the 9,920 lb (4,500 kg) of ballast for the two-wheel pull test. In addition, Denza added small stabilizers to each axle so the vehicle remained balanced on two wheels.

After each run, the vehicle was inspected and confirmed to show no signs of stress on the powertrain, chassis, or tires.

The Bao 5 SUV normally has a towing capacity of over 5,500 lbs (2,500 kg), according to BYD’s Denza brand.
